title: Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: Peter and Paul absolutely predestined to life and to the whole series of means — will of end absolutely joined to will of means
pass_a_gloss: We say that Peter, Paul, and the rest are absolutely predestined unto eternal life, not that they themselves before they believe absolutely know this decree of God, or that they themselves obtain eternal life the condition of faith being in no wise performed; but that they are elected by God absolutely and gratuitously, not only unto eternal life itself, but unto the whole series of means by which they are brought unto it. Although therefore in the execution of the end it hangs upon the conditional use of means, yet in God predestinating Peter, Paul, or any singular person, the will of the end was not conditioned, but absolutely connected with the will of the means; so that by one and the same most simple act by which God willed glory unto Peter or Paul, he also willed faith, and all the rest from whose conditional use glory is promised. In a word, God did not decree to save Peter without the condition of faith, but as absolutely and precisely decreed to give faith unto Peter as salvation. And this is what is commonly said, that Predestination is the preparation of grace in the present, and of glory in the future.
pass_b_english: We say Peter, Paul, and the rest are absolutely predestined to eternal life — not that they know that decree absolutely before they believe, or that they gain eternal life with the faith-condition never performed — but that God elects them absolutely and freely not only to eternal life itself but to the whole series of means by which they are brought to it. In execution the end hangs on conditional use of means; yet in God predestining Peter, Paul, or any particular person, the will of the end was not conditioned but absolutely joined to the will of the means — so that by one and the same simplest act by which God willed glory for Peter or Paul he also willed faith and all else from whose conditional use glory is promised. In a word: God did not decree to save Peter without the condition of faith, but decreed to give Peter faith as absolutely and precisely as salvation. That is the common saying: Predestination is preparation of grace now and of glory hereafter.
source_text: Nos dicimus, Petrum, Paulum, reliquosque ad vitam aeternam absolute praedestinatos, non quod ipsi antequam credant absolute sciant hoc Dei decretum, aut quod ipsi vitam aeternam consequantur fidei conditione minime praestita; sed quod a Deo absolute et gratuito eliguntur, non modo ad ipsam vitam aeternam, sed ad totam seriem mediorum quibus ad eam perducuntur. Licet itaque in exsecutione finis pendeat a conditionali usu mediorum, tamen in Deo praedestinante Petrum, Paulum, aut quamcunque personam singularem, voluntas finis non fuit conditionata, sed absolute connexa cum voluntate mediorum; ita ut uno et eodem simplicissimo actu, quo Deus voluit Petro aut Paulo gloriam, voluerit etiam et fidem, ceteraque omnia ex quorum usu conditionali gloria promittitur. Uno verbo, Deus non decrevit servare Petrum sine conditione fidei, sed tam absolute et precise fidem Petro dare decrevit, quam salutem. Atque hoc est quod vulgo dicitur, Praedestinationem esse praeparationem gratiae in praesenti, et gloriae in futuro.
